definitions.explanation: Actively supporting and defending a person, cause, or right, especially against criticism or opposition. Implies standing up for something one believes in.

examples.japanese: {人権|じんけん}を{擁護|ようご}する。
{彼|かれ}は{憲法|けんぽう}{改正|かいせい}に{反対|はんたい}し、{現行|げんこう}{憲法|けんぽう}の{擁護|ようご}を{訴|うった}えた。
examples.english: He opposed the constitutional amendment and called for the defense of the current constitution.

examples.japanese: スキャンダルの{中|なか}でも{社長|しゃちょう}を{擁護|ようご}する{社員|しゃいん}がいた。
examples.english: Even in the midst of the scandal, some employees defended the president.

notes:
A formal word often used in legal, political, and human rights contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人権|じんけん}{擁護|ようご} (human rights advocacy)
- {憲法|けんぽう}{擁護|ようご} (defending the constitution)
- {擁護|ようご}{派|は} (supporters, defenders — a faction)
- {擁護|ようご}する{立場|たちば} (a position of defending/supporting)

USAGE NOTE:
{擁護|ようご} implies taking a stance and actively defending something against attack or criticism. It is stronger than {支持|しじ} (support), which can be passive. {弁護|べんご} (legal defense) is more specific to courtroom settings.
